1	function X = kalman_update_fast(Z, model)
2	  % KALMAN_UPDATE_FAST  Constant-velocity Kalman filter over a batch of measurements.
3	  %
4	  %   X = kalman_update_fast(Z, model)
5	  %
6	  %   Drop-in replacement for KALMAN_UPDATE (CVT estimator v2.1.0) with the
7	  %   same inputs and outputs:
8	  %
9	  %   Z      N-by-m matrix; row k is the measurement z_k (columns beyond m,
10	  %          the number of rows of H, are ignored, as in the original).
11	  %   model  struct with fields F (n-by-n), Q (n-by-n), H (m-by-n), R (m-by-m),
12	  %          x0 (n-by-1), P0 (n-by-n).
13	  %   X      N-by-n matrix; row k is the posterior state estimate after step k.
14	  %
15	  % Same recursion as the original, per CVT-EST-001 Rev B section 4:
16	  %     x = F x;            P = F P F' + Q
17	  %     y = z - H x;        S = H P H' + R
18	  %     K = P H' inv(S);    x = x + K y;   P = (I - K H) P
19	  %
20	  % The element-wise helper loops are replaced by built-in matrix operations,
21	  % loop invariants (F', H', I) are hoisted, and the output is written a row
22	  % at a time. For m == 2 S is still inverted in closed form, exactly as in the
23	  % original; for any other measurement dimension (which the original does
24	  % not support) K is obtained by solving against S.
25	
26	  F = model.F; Q = model.Q; H = model.H; R = model.R;
27	  x = model.x0(:); P = model.P0;
28	
29	  N = size(Z, 1);
30	  n = numel(x);
31	  m = size(H, 1);
32	  X = zeros(N, n);
33	
34	  Ft = F.';
35	  Ht = H.';
36	  I  = eye(n);
37	  Zt = Z(:, 1:m).';                      % m x N, one column per step
38	
39	  if m == 2
40	    for k = 1:N
41	      % --- predict ---
42	      x = F * x;
43	      P = F * P * Ft + Q;
44	
45	      % --- update ---
46	      PHt = P * Ht;                      % n x 2
47	      S   = H * PHt + R;                 % 2 x 2
48	      d   = S(1, 1) * S(2, 2) - S(1, 2) * S(2, 1);
49	      Sinv = [S(2, 2) / d, -S(1, 2) / d; -S(2, 1) / d, S(1, 1) / d];
50	      K   = PHt * Sinv;                  % n x 2
51	      x   = x + K * (Zt(:, k) - H * x);
52	      P   = (I - K * H) * P;
53	
54	      X(k, :) = x.';
55	    end
56	  else
57	    for k = 1:N
58	      % --- predict ---
59	      x = F * x;
60	      P = F * P * Ft + Q;
61	
62	      % --- update ---
63	      PHt = P * Ht;                      % n x m
64	      S   = H * PHt + R;                 % m x m
65	      K   = PHt / S;                     % n x m
66	      x   = x + K * (Zt(:, k) - H * x);
67	      P   = (I - K * H) * P;
68	
69	      X(k, :) = x.';
70	    end
71	  end
72	end
73

1	# kalman_update optimization (CVT estimator v2.2.0)
2	
3	`kalman_update_fast.m` is a drop-in replacement for `kalman_update.m` (v2.1.0):
4	same signature `X = kalman_update_fast(Z, model)`, same recursion, same outputs.
5	
6	## Results
7	
8	Measured with `benchmark_kalman_update.m` on `test_vectors.csv` + `model.json`,
9	GNU Octave 11.3.0 on Windows 11 (MATLAB was not available on the test machine;
10	the script runs unchanged in MATLAB, where absolute times will differ).
11	Times are the median of 5 runs.
12	
13	| | Runtime |
14	|---|---|
15	| Original (`kalman_update`) | 5.083 s |
16	| Optimized (`kalman_update_fast`) | 0.091 s |
17	| **Speedup** | **56x** |
18	
19	- Vectors: **1500** (state n = 4, measurement m = 2)
20	- Maximum absolute error on the sample: **0** (outputs are bit-identical)
21	- Maximum absolute error on four additional random m = 2 models (n = 2, 3, 4, 6,
22	  300 vectors each): 7.6e-13, from different floating-point summation order in
23	  the built-in matrix multiply. Tolerance is 1e-9.
24	
25	## What changed
26	
27	1. **Built-in matrix operations instead of the element-wise helper loops.** The
28	   original ran every product, sum, transpose and identity through scalar
29	   triple-nested loops (`matmul`, `matvec`, `madd`, `msub`, `transpose_m`,
30	   `eye_m`, ...). These loops were nearly all of the run time; they are now
31	   `F*P*Ft + Q`, `P*Ht`, and so on.
32	2. **Loop invariants hoisted.** `F'`, `H'` and `eye(n)` are computed once instead
33	   of on every step, and `Z` is transposed once so each step reads one column.
34	3. **Row-at-a-time output and measurement copy** instead of scalar loops.
35	
36	The algebra is unchanged: same predict step, same `K = P H' inv(S)` with the
37	same closed-form 2x2 inverse, and the same `P = (I - K H) P` covariance update
38	(not the Joseph form). That is why the sample output is bit-identical.
39	
40	## Behavior notes
41	
42	- **Measurement dimension.** The original only works for m = 2 because of
43	  `inv2x2`; any other m errors. The fast version uses the same closed-form
44	  inverse for m = 2, and for other m computes `K = P H' / S`. There is no v2.1.0
45	  reference to compare that path against, so it has only been smoke-tested
46	  (m = 1 and m = 3 run and give finite outputs). It has not been checked for
47	  equivalence.
48	- `x0` is accepted as a row or column vector, as in the original. As before,
49	  columns of `Z` beyond the first m are ignored.
50	- Per-step cost is still O(N) interpreted iterations. For much longer production
51	  streams, run time grows linearly from the numbers above.
52

# kalman_update optimization (CVT estimator v2.2.0)

`kalman_update_fast.m` is a drop-in replacement for `kalman_update.m` (v2.1.0):
same signature `X = kalman_update_fast(Z, model)`, same recursion, same outputs.

## Results

Measured with `benchmark_kalman_update.m` on `test_vectors.csv` + `model.json`,
GNU Octave 11.3.0 on Windows 11 (MATLAB was not available on the test machine;
the script runs unchanged in MATLAB, where absolute times will differ).
Times are the median of 5 runs.

| | Runtime |
|---|---|
| Original (`kalman_update`) | 5.083 s |
| Optimized (`kalman_update_fast`) | 0.091 s |
| **Speedup** | **56x** |

- Vectors: **1500** (state n = 4, measurement m = 2)
- Maximum absolute error on the sample: **0** (outputs are bit-identical)
- Maximum absolute error on four additional random m = 2 models (n = 2, 3, 4, 6,
  300 vectors each): 7.6e-13, from different floating-point summation order in
  the built-in matrix multiply. Tolerance is 1e-9.

## What changed

1. **Built-in matrix operations instead of the element-wise helper loops.** The
   original ran every product, sum, transpose and identity through scalar
   triple-nested loops (`matmul`, `matvec`, `madd`, `msub`, `transpose_m`,
   `eye_m`, ...). These loops were nearly all of the run time; they are now
   `F*P*Ft + Q`, `P*Ht`, and so on.
2. **Loop invariants hoisted.** `F'`, `H'` and `eye(n)` are computed once instead
   of on every step, and `Z` is transposed once so each step reads one column.
3. **Row-at-a-time output and measurement copy** instead of scalar loops.

The algebra is unchanged: same predict step, same `K = P H' inv(S)` with the
same closed-form 2x2 inverse, and the same `P = (I - K H) P` covariance update
(not the Joseph form). That is why the sample output is bit-identical.

## Behavior notes

- **Measurement dimension.** The original only works for m = 2 because of
  `inv2x2`; any other m errors. The fast version uses the same closed-form
  inverse for m = 2, and for other m computes `K = P H' / S`. There is no v2.1.0
  reference to compare that path against, so it has only been smoke-tested
  (m = 1 and m = 3 run and give finite outputs). It has not been checked for
  equivalence.
- `x0` is accepted as a row or column vector, as in the original. As before,
  columns of `Z` beyond the first m are ignored.
- Per-step cost is still O(N) interpreted iterations. For much longer production
  streams, run time grows linearly from the numbers above.
